hook.line: A message that says what happened is fine. A message that says why, and what happens next, is one people actually answer. Spanish has four little joiners for that.
hook.es: Como Altamira compró el edificio, Tomás está preocupado.
hook.en: Since Altamira bought the building, Tomás is worried.

examples.es: No voy porque no tengo plata.
examples.en: I'm not going because I don't have any money.
As it was raining, we didn't go out.

examples.es: No tengo plata, por eso no voy.
examples.en: I don't have any money, that's why I'm not going.

examples.es: Estoy cansado, así que me voy.
examples.en: I'm tired, so I'm leaving. (a man speaking)

examples.es: El café cerró temprano porque no había clientes.

examples.es:
¿Por qué estás cansada?
Porque trabajé mucho.
examples.en:
Why are you tired? (to a woman friend)
Because I worked a lot.

rule:
Two words give the reason:
*porque*, because: after the main news. *No voy porque no tengo plata.*
*como*, since or as: at the very start. *Como llovía, no salimos.*

Two words give the result:
*por eso*, that's why
*así que*, so
They come second, after a comma: *No tengo plata, por eso no voy.*

The one to watch is *como*. English can put since at the end; Spanish *como* only works at the front. If the reason comes second, switch to *porque*.

And don't mix up the question with the answer. *¿Por qué?* is two words with an accent: why. *Porque* is one word, no accent: because.
smallPrint: Teachers call *porque* and *como* causal connectors, and *por eso* and *así que* consecutive (result) connectors.

readAndPick.es: Tomás está cansado, por eso Vale abre el café.
options: Tomás is tired, that's why Vale is opening the café.
Vale is opening the café, that's why Tomás is tired.

readAndPick.es: Vale está cansada porque abre el café.
options: Vale is opening the café because she's tired.
Vale is tired because she opens the café.

readAndPick.es: Como Hernando no vino, Mariana trabajó en el café.
options: Since Mariana worked at the café, Hernando didn't come.
Since Hernando didn't come, Mariana worked at the café.

readAndPick.es: Mariana no vino porque trabajó mucho.
options: Mariana didn't come because she worked a lot.
Mariana worked a lot because she didn't come.

readAndPick.es: Hernando no vino, así que Mariana trabajó en el café.
options: Mariana worked at the café, so Hernando didn't come.
Hernando came, but Mariana worked at the café.
Hernando didn't come, so Mariana worked at the café.
Why are you sad?
Because you're sad.
Why are you sad?
Because you're sad.

readAndPick.es: Como no tengo plata, no compro el carro.
options: I'm not buying the car, so I have money.
Since I don't have any money, I'm not buying the car.
I don't have money because I bought the car.

readAndPick.es: El negocio no va bien, así que Tomás necesita un plan.
options: Tomás needs a plan because the business is doing well.
Tomás has a plan, so the business is doing well.
The business isn't doing well, so Tomás needs a plan.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ llovía, no salimos.* (*Como* or *Porque*) As it was raining, we didn't go out.
yourTurn.why: The reason comes first, so it's *como*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No salimos ___ llovía.* (*como* or *porque*) We didn't go out because it was raining.
yourTurn.why: The reason comes second, so it's *porque*.

yourTurn.prompt: I don't have any money, that's why I'm not going.
yourTurn.answer: No tengo plata, por eso no voy.
accept: No tengo dinero, por eso no voy.
yourTurn.why: That's why is *por eso*, after a comma.

yourTurn.prompt: I'm tired, so I'm going home. (a man speaking)
yourTurn.answer: Estoy cansado, así que voy a la casa.
accept: Estoy cansado, así que voy a casa.
Estoy cansado, así que me voy a la casa.
Estoy cansado, así que me voy a casa.
yourTurn.why: So, for a result, is *así que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a woman friend: Why are you tired?
yourTurn.why: Why is two words with an accent: *¿Por qué…?*

yourTurn.prompt: Start with *como*: *No fui porque estaba enfermo.* (a man speaking)
yourTurn.why: *Como* puts the reason first, then a comma, then what happened.

yourTurn.prompt: Use *por eso*: *Vale abre el café porque Tomás está cansado.*
yourTurn.answer: Tomás está cansado, por eso Vale abre el café.
yourTurn.why: With *por eso* you start from the reason and land on the result.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Como* only works at the front; when the reason comes second, use *porque*.
Why, the question, is two words with an accent: *por qué*.

pitfalls.right: Estoy cansado, así que me voy.
pitfalls.why: So is *así que*; *así* on its own means like this.

personal: Write one true sentence with a reason (*…porque…*) and one with a result (*…, así que…*) about your week.
